newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Taleban send reinforcements to eastern Afghanistan.
newsitem.headline: Taleban send reinforcements to eastern Afghanistan.

text.p: The Islamic Taleban have sent troop reinforcements to eastern Afghanistan to fight the ousted government's forces after suffering recent setbacks in the region, a Taleban official said on Monday.

Maulvi Sadar Azam, Taleban deputy governor of Nangarhar province, told the Afghan Islamic Press that forces loyal to ousted President Burhanuddin Rabbani captured the Manogi district in Pich valley of Kunar province three days ago.

He told the news agency, based in the Pakistani city of Peshawar, that the Taleban had already sent reinforcements to the region, which is near the border with northern Pakistan and about 60 km (35 miles) north of Jalalabad city.
"Fighting has started against the opponents and, God willing, we will sweep them," Azam said.
Azam said at least 500 Taleban troops had also been sent from Kandahar in southern Afghanistan to face a possible threat to the eastern provinces of Nangarhar and Kunar.
The Taleban have set up several new posts to protect the provinces from attack, he said.
Tension in the east follows what Taleban officials said was the killing last week by pro-Rabbani forces of a captured Taleban leader and an unknown number of his colleagues.
Maulvi Gulzar, commissioner of Dara-i-Noor town in Nangarhar province, was seized along with others when pro-Rabbani forces overran the area, 50 km (30 miles) north of Jalalabad.
A Taleban official said Gulzar and an undetermined number of his colleagues were shot dead while attempting to escape.
